_meta.indication: VIBERZI is indicated in adults for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, multi-national, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 52 weeks in duration (26-week controlled treatment then continued double-blinded to 52 weeks for long-term safety)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) meeting worst abdominal pain >3.0 and BSS >=5.5 entry criteria
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of composite responders over the initial 12-week double-blind period (simultaneous daily improvement of worst abdominal pain by >=30% and stool consistency BSS <5 on >=50% of days)
pivotal_trials.result: Composite responder rate over 12 weeks: 25% (100 mg) vs 17% placebo; treatment difference 8% (95% CI 2.6, 13.5), P<0.01

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multi-center, multi-national, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 26-week treatment period followed by a 4-week single-blinded placebo-withdrawal period
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of composite responders over the initial 12-week double-blind period
pivotal_trials.result: Composite responder rate over 12 weeks: 30% (100 mg) vs 16% placebo; treatment difference 13% (95% CI 7.5, 19.2), P<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>5%) are constipation (8% at 100 mg vs 3% placebo), nausea (7% vs 5% placebo) and abdominal pain (7% vs 4% placebo). Serious risks include sphincter of Oddi spasm (0.8% at 100 mg) and pancreatitis.
target_moa: Eluxadoline is a mu-opioid receptor agonist, delta-opioid receptor antagonist, and kappa-opioid receptor agonist that acts locally on opioid receptors in the gut

rems.type: No REMS was required; FDA concluded no safety issue identified justified a REMS

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened to discuss this application

basis.text: The IND was granted fast track designation in January 2011

citations.quote: The IND was submitted in November 2007, and was granted fast track designation in January 2011.

summary.text: Eluxadoline, a new molecular entity for IBS-D, was granted fast track designation in January 2011 and approved via a standard (non-accelerated) full approval; no advisory committee was convened and no REMS was required. It was recommended for Schedule IV placement under the Controlled Substances Act.
